item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 311124
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Mon Aug 31 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Karina, located well west-southwest of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula, and on Tropical Storm Lowell, located well
east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands.

Well Offshore of Southwestern Mexico (EP95):
Showers and thunderstorms are showing signs of organization in
association with a broad area of low pressure located several
hundred miles south-southwest of the coast of southwestern Mexico.
Environmental conditions are conducive for development, and a
tropical depression or tropical storm is expected to form later
today or tonight, while the system moves northwestward around 10
mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...90 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south or southwest of the
Hawaiian Islands in a couple of days. Some gradual development is
possible thereafter while it moves slowly and erratically.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Hurricane Karina Public Advisory Number 17
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM HST Mon Aug 31 2026 
000
WTPZ31 KNHC 311455
TCPEP1
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Karina Advisory Number  17
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
500 AM HST Mon Aug 31 2026
 
...KARINA CONTINUES TO MOVE WESTWARD OVER THE OPEN WATERS OF THE
TROPICAL EASTERN PACIFIC...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 500 AM HST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...17.4N 125.1W
ABOUT 1055 MI...1700 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...140 MPH...220 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 275 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...950 MB...28.06 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 500 AM HST (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Karina was located
near latitude 17.4 North, longitude 125.1 West. Karina is moving
toward the west near 9 mph (15 km/h), and this motion is
expected to continue through the rest of today. A turn toward the
west-northwest is forecast on Tuesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 130 mph (215 km/h)
with higher gusts. Karina is a category 4 hurricane on the
Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale. Fluctuations in intensity
remain possible today, and a gradual weakening trend is expected to
begin on Tuesday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 30 miles (45 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 115 miles
(185 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 950 mb (28.06 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Karina will affect portions of the coast
of southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula for the next
couple of days and will likely spread northward to southern
California on Monday through midweek. These swells are likely to
cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 1100 AM HST.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Roberts

item.title: Hurricane Karina Forecast Discussion Number 17
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM HST Mon Aug 31 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 311455
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Karina Discussion Number  17
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
500 AM HST Mon Aug 31 2026
 
Conventional satellite imagery shows that the inner core structure
of Karina has become a little less defined.  The cloud tops in
the northwestern portion of the eyewall have warmed to around -60
C, and the latest TAFB Dvorak satellite intensity estimate is
T5.5/102 kt.  The CMISS satellite intensity objective techniques 
range from 115 to 129 kt.  Based on these data, the initial
intensity remains at 120 kt.
 
Karina continues to move generally westward, estimated at 275
degrees at 7 kt. A narrow but extensive mid-level ridge is parked
to the north of the hurricane, and this feature will likely remain
the dominant steering impact on Karina over the next several days.
Toward the end of the forecast period, the original ridge becomes
eroded by a mid-latitude trough digging into the western US coast,
but a more meridionally oriented ridge takes its place to the
northwest of Karina, which should act to gradually slow its forward
motion.  The current NHC forecast track has been adjusted
slightly to the south of the previous track based on the guidance
from the HFIP Corrected Consensus Approach (HCCA) and Google
DeepMind (GDMI) guidance.
 
While environmental conditions should remain favorable in the short
term, the hurricane could experience some intensity fluctuations due
to inner-core changes.  Karina may develop annular characteristics
that could help reduce the rate of weakening the cyclone is forecast
to undergo. The current SHIPS statistical intensity models indicate
that relative humidity beyond 72 h will drop below 40%, 
Consequently, abundant dry, stable air will impact the hurricane.   
Once Karina moves over cooler ocean waters past 96 h, and more dry 
air is pulled into the hurricane's inner core, the rate of 
weakening could increase at a faster rate indicated in the 
official forecast which is close to the HCCA corrected consensus.
 
Karina's wind radii have been adjusted based on 0553 UTC METOP-B/C
ASCAT overpasses, and 0757 UTC OSCAT data.
